geopolitics_summary: EU sanctions on Russian energy tightened (price cap frozen); Strait of Hormuz security tensions rising; Spanish/French wildfires amplify climate/insurance cost risks.

themes.headline: Greek concession unlocks EU Russia sanctions; price cap frozen 12 months
themes.why_it_matters: Price cap freeze on Russian crude weakens LNG arbitrage pressure into EU; resolves shipping dispute on Russian gas to third countries—reduces supply-shock risk to TTF winter curve.

themes.headline: Spanish wildfires 20× more likely due to climate change; 100k+ displaced
themes.why_it_matters: Massive fires in Spain/France risk damage to power infrastructure, hydro/wind assets, and grid stability. Cascading blackout risk + forced outages tighten near-term power balances; DA spreads vulnerable.

themes.headline: Mexico's Energia Costa Azul LNG terminal ships first Phase 1 cargo
themes.why_it_matters: New 0.4 Bcf/d LNG supply into Atlantic basin increases arbitrage pressure on EU TTF; marginal LNG cargoes diverted to US/Mexico rather than NW Europe caps upside risk on winter curve.

themes.headline: Trump bans foreign-made robots, power inverters; cites Chinese influence risk
themes.why_it_matters: US supply-chain restrictions on power inverters/grid gear may disrupt European grid modernization, renewables curtailment control, and carbon market credibility if grid resilience worsens. Indirect EUA pressure.

themes.headline: Trump urges UK/France lead Strait of Hormuz patrol; allies hesitant
themes.why_it_matters: Strait tensions unresolved; potential for oil supply disruption increases implied LNG scarcity risk. Higher crude → fuel-switching fuel cost advantage erodes, supporting power prices via gas-power substitution.

watchlist: Spain wildfire containment & power asset damage assessments (next 3–5 days).
EU LNG arbitrage flows; Mexico Energia Costa Azul ramp-up impact on TTF (weeks).
Strait of Hormuz escalation; crude price/LNG arb risk (ongoing).
France presidential election & energy policy shifts; ministry stability (Q4 2026–2027).
